question: A 45-year-old man with HIV comes to the physician because of multiple lesions on his chest and lower extremities. The lesions have progressively increased in size and are not painful or pruritic. Current medications include abacavir, dolutegravir, and lamivudine. A photograph of the lesions is shown. His CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 450/mm3 (normal ≥ 500/mm3). A skin biopsy shows multiple spindle-shaped cells and lymphocytic infiltrate. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "HIV infection" -> "CD4+ T-lymphocyte count of 450/mm3" -> "Immune compromise" -> "Increased risk of opportunistic infections" -> "Kaposi sarcoma" -> "Spindle-shaped cells and lymphocytic infiltrate on skin biopsy" -> "Kaposi sarcoma treatment required" -> "Alpha-interferon" -> 85%

enhanced_information: In a 45-year-old man with HIV and Kaposi sarcoma, the most appropriate pharmacotherapy is Alpha-interferon. This treatment is indicated for Kaposi sarcoma due to its ability to inhibit viral replication and enhance the immune response. Evidence supports the use of Interferon-alpha in boosting immunity, aligning with the consensus for treating this condition.
analysis: Kaposi sarcoma is a common malignancy seen in patients with HIV. The most appropriate pharmacotherapy for Kaposi sarcoma in this patient is Alpha-interferon, as it can inhibit viral replication and enhance the immune response.
